items.headline: G7 Agrees to Release 100 Million Barrels of Emergency Oil Reserves
items.summary: On October 2, Group of Seven leaders agreed to release 100 million barrels of crude oil and fuel from emergency reserves over four months, prioritizing an immediate release of diesel. The coordinated measure was launched to stabilize volatile energy markets and curb surging fuel prices caused by ongoing geopolitical conflicts.

items.headline: Google Launches AI Chips into Orbit to Test Space Data Centers
items.summary: Google launched four custom artificial intelligence processing chips into low Earth orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket as part of its experimental Project Suncatcher mission. The trial is testing whether AI hardware can withstand cosmic radiation and harsh thermal conditions to see if orbital data centers are feasible.

items.headline: A'ja Wilson Powers Las Vegas Aces Past Indiana Fever into WNBA Semifinals
items.summary: A'ja Wilson delivered 36 points and 10 rebounds to lead the Las Vegas Aces to a 94–83 Game 3 victory over Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever. The decisive win eliminated Indiana from the postseason and propelled the defending champion Aces into the WNBA semifinals.

items.headline: Oasis Blocks Auction of Unheard 1990s Recording Archive
items.summary: British rock band Oasis filed legal action to halt the planned auction of 'The Desk Tapes,' a rare archive containing over 100 hours of 1990s live performances, rehearsals, and private band conversations. Littleton Auctions confirmed the collection was withdrawn after the band sued their former sound engineer and his son over intellectual property rights.
